answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by using an anchor of slow, costly history instead of free signup: a new agent starts with no trust and must complete small, verifiable tasks for distinct, already-trusted peers, whose endorsements accumulate like a reef built coral by coral. Creating thousands of fake identities gains nothing, because each one must separately earn that record, and no ivory credential or self-issued badge can substitute for diverse, independent vouches over time.
